Interview prompt: "Walk me through a time you improved a system's resilience to a third-party dependency."
fields.Back:
S: BMO's loan/mortgage submission flow called a third-party credit-check service directly, so a slow or failing check could cascade into submission failures.
T: Decouple submission from the credit-check dependency so one failure mode couldn't take down the other.
A: Architected a serverless event-driven backend using AWS Lambda + EventBridge — submission logic published events instead of calling the credit-check service synchronously.
R: Reduced coupling by 40% and eliminated cascading failures between the two systems.

fields.Front: Interview prompt: "Describe a full-stack feature you owned end to end."
fields.Back:
S: BMO needed a Mortgage & Loan Calculator web app for branch/customer use.
T: Build and later modernize it end to end, frontend to data layer.
A: Built the app with Angular/TypeScript on Node.js/AWS, then owned migrating the frontend to a React SPA and designing a new DynamoDB schema.
R: The migration made processing 60% faster while keeping the app on AWS-native infrastructure.

fields.Text: The Mortgage & Loan Calculator was built end-to-end using {{c1::Angular}} and {{c2::TypeScript}} on the frontend, with {{c3::Node.js}} on AWS for the backend.

Michele architected a serverless event-driven backend with {{c1::AWS Lambda}} + {{c2::EventBridge}} to decouple submission logic from third-party credit checks, cutting coupling by {{c3::40%}} and preventing {{c4::cascading failures}}.

fields.Back: An AWS event bus service used to route events between decoupled services (e.g. loan submission → credit check) instead of direct synchronous calls.
